hypothesis: A normalized asset catalog and data-only view definitions can replace both Scope frontends while preserving canonical evidence and enabling project-specific views

actions.text: Inventory canonical assets and define a versioned catalog and projection configuration
Replace Scope presentation and integrate configured offline and live rendering using the existing libraries
Exercise customization, evidence preservation, invalid configuration, live updates and packaged rendering

criteria.text: Every inventoried asset family is addressable with attributes and source availability
A project can add and modify graph table and card projections without frontend code
Tests and browser checks demonstrate offline and live operation with the shipped default

actionResults.evidence: Implemented and documented 50 asset kinds, complete spec-section capture, attributes, explicit relationships, source availability and versioned JSON view configuration.
Replaced the CLI canvas and separate preview panels with one packaged React/Radix/React Flow/Cytoscape viewer; added offline generation, live serving and in-browser configuration preview.

The full suite passed 1038 tests; the final focused Scope suite passed 13 tests after the last relationship additions; Chromium and WebKit browser checks, final package smoke, fast verification, typecheck, both host controls, docs check and diff check passed.

criterionResults.evidence: The registry-wide selection test exercises all 50 kinds; canonical capture tests cover structure, specs, work, defects, journal identity, incomplete receipts and source damage; the real repository captures more than 8300 assets.
Browser and packed-consumer tests apply custom graph/table/card definitions from JSON without frontend changes, including replacing all default tabs and rejecting invalid configuration.

Both browser engines exercise all default views, 12-component readable layout, offline network silence, live project configuration and source updates, ignored pinned-evidence changes, pause/resume and damaged-config recovery.

hypothesis: A repository design thesis can preserve the complete agreed Structure direction and make the next implementation concrete without claiming proposed capabilities already exist

actions.text: Write a detailed thesis covering the agreed experience, canonical data and spec needs, renderer and MCP contracts, comparison, implementation stages and acceptance scenarios
Review the thesis against the conversation and current source, validate local links and whitespace, and distinguish open design choices from settled requirements

criteria.text: The thesis contains every final user requirement and does not revive rejected file cards, import arrows or default comparisons
Current capabilities, proposed interfaces, pending decisions and acceptance evidence are explicitly separated, and local document links resolve

actionResults.evidence: Wrote docs/scope-structure-thesis.md, a 7475-word thesis with 22 sections covering the complete Structure design, current implementation seams, proposed contracts, staged delivery and acceptance criteria.

Reviewed the final requirements against the design conversation and current catalog, capture, configuration, layout, app, guarantee identity and lifecycle code. Checked all 29 local and section links, balanced code fences, illustrative JSON and whitespace.

criterionResults.evidence: The agreed-requirements table and detailed sections preserve spec density, architectural stacks without file cards or bare import arrows, independent zoom detail, spec-owned relationships, guarantees, taxa, uncertainty, sidebar, current-state opening, explicit comparisons with ghosted removals and MCP control.

The thesis explicitly separates the current generic implementation from proposed renderer/configuration/MCP APIs, retains a pending-decisions table, marks illustrative relationships and change summaries, and defines unclaimed acceptance criteria. All 29 links resolve; no runtime behavior changed.
